role_or_event: Birth (born Darlene Lettie Graham)
description: Born in Central, South Carolina, to Florence James ('F. J.') Graham and Millie Graham (nee Walters).

role_or_event: Family business childhood
description: Parents operated a restaurant, bar, liquor store and pool hall; the family lived in rooms behind the business.

role_or_event: Orphaned in childhood
description: Mother died of cancer when Graham was 11; father died of a heart attack 15 months later. Exact dates not stated in the retrieved source.

role_or_event: Moved in with an aunt and uncle
description: After her parents' deaths her brother Lindsey arranged for her to live with an aunt and uncle in Seneca, South Carolina.

role_or_event: Legal guardianship by Lindsey Graham
description: Lindsey Graham, nine years her senior, became her legal guardian before joining the Air Force in 1982; he also taught her to spell her first name 'Darline'.

role_or_event: Bachelor of Science in sociology
description: Graduated with a BS in sociology in 1989.

role_or_event: Appeared in a television advertisement for her brother's Senate campaign
description: Appeared in a 2002 TV ad for Lindsey Graham's U.S. Senate campaign; assisted him in subsequent campaigns and discussed her childhood during the 2014 and 2026 Senate races.

role_or_event: Staff, South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department
description: Began working for the department in 2007; helped coordinate a remote work program for adults with severe disabilities for Time Warner.

role_or_event: Master of Arts in rehabilitation counseling
description: Earned an MA in rehabilitation counseling in 2009; is also a certified public manager.

role_or_event: Public information director, South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department
description: Was the department's public information director in 2015.

role_or_event: Introduced her brother at his first presidential campaign speech
description: Supported her brother's 2016 presidential campaign and introduced him at his first campaign speech.

role_or_event: Commissioner and agency head, South Carolina Commission for the Blind
organization: South Carolina Commission for the Blind
description: Became commissioner and agency head in September 2019; the agency administers vocational rehabilitation, independent living and blindness-prevention programs. Predecessor James Kirby; successor (acting) Luis Gamarra Mendoza.

role_or_event: Member, South Carolina State Workforce Development Board
organization: South Carolina State Workforce Development Board
description: Serves on the state workforce development board and its works management committee.

role_or_event: President-elect, National Council of State Agencies for the Blind
organization: National Council of State Agencies for the Blind
description: Became president-elect in 2026; term scheduled to begin in January 2027.

role_or_event: Appointed to the U.S. Senate by Governor Henry McMaster
organization: Office of the Governor of South Carolina
description: Appointed on July 13, 2026 to fill the vacancy created by the death of her brother Lindsey Graham, on the recommendation of President Donald Trump; Trump endorsed her the same day.

role_or_event: Sworn in as U.S. Senator from South Carolina
description: Sworn in on July 14, 2026; first woman to represent South Carolina in the Senate and first sister to replace a sibling in the Senate.

role_or_event: Introduced the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
description: Introduced legislation to impose sanctions on Russia, based on the Sanctioning Russia Act authored by Lindsey Graham; it passed the Senate in August and the House in mid-September with bipartisan support and was signed into law by President Trump two days later.

role_or_event: Publicly encouraged by President Trump to run for a full term
description: Trump publicly encouraged Graham on July 17 to run in the 2026 Senate election and promised to endorse her if she did.

role_or_event: Announced candidacy for a full Senate term
description: Told Sean Hannity three days later that she intended to run for a full term; announced on July 20 that she would run.

role_or_event: Finished first in the special Republican primary
description: Came in first in the August 11 special primary and advanced to a runoff with Ralph Norman.

role_or_event: Won the special Republican primary runoff
description: Won the August 25 runoff against Ralph Norman and advanced to the general election.

role_or_event: Voted to confirm Todd Blanche as U.S. Attorney General
description: Voted to confirm Blanche, who was approved 50-49; reported by WPDE on August 8, 2026. Exact vote date not stated in the retrieved source.

role_or_event: Senate committee assignments
description: Assigned to Appropriations (with six subcommittees), Budget, Environment and Public Works, and the Judiciary.

role_or_event: Lost the general election for the U.S. Senate
description: Lost to Democratic nominee Annie Andrews on November 3, 2026, in what the retrieved source describes as an upset.
